proposed_widenings.name: reposition_attachment
proposed_widenings.justification: The caster can spend a Magic action on any turn while the spell persists to move the illusion to any other spot within range. The on_caster_spends_action trigger (standard_action: magic) exists and fits perfectly, but the resulting operation — repositioning the effect's spatial anchor to a new point within range — has no corresponding atom. force_move and teleport apply only to creatures; alter_item_kind applies to item forms. No atom moves a non-creature effect attachment to a new location. Identical gap identified in Dancing Lights and Major Image.
proposed_widenings.evidence: As a Magic action, you can cause the image to move to any spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image.

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingTrigger.on_creature_studies
proposed_widenings.justification: The disbelief mechanic fires when a creature spends a Study action to examine the illusion, triggering an Intelligence (Investigation) check against the spell save DC. No OngoingTrigger variant covers a creature spending a specific named action (Study) to examine the effect. The closest existing trigger is on_attached_turn_start (unconditional) or on_caster_spends_action (caster-side). A new trigger variant is needed for 'creature spends Study action on the attachment'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A creature that takes a Study action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC.

notes: Core mechanic encodes cleanly: create_illusion (huge, visual only) as a passive ongoing operation over an area (15-ft cube) attachment at point_within_range. Typecheck passes; tracer emits a valid graph. Identical structure to Major Image (level 3, gargantuan, all four sensory channels) — same two widenings apply. The disbelief check is a secondary mechanic present on all illusion spells; the reposition_attachment gap is the primary atom missing from v4.
